4.1.2 Conditions
We compared six conditions including GraphRAG at four different graph community levels ( C0,
C1, C2, C3), a text summarization method that applies our map-reduce approach directly to source
texts (TS), and a vector RAG “semantic search” approach (SS):
• CO. Uses root-level community summaries (fewest in number) to answer user queries.
• C1. Uses high-level community summaries to answer queries. These are sub-communities
of C0, if present, otherwise C0 communities projected downwards.
• C2. Uses intermediate-level community summaries to answer queries. These are sub-
communities of C1, if present, otherwise C1 communities projected downwards.
• C3. Uses low-level community summaries (greatest in number) to answer queries. These
are sub-communities of C2, if present, otherwise C2 communities projected downwards.
• TS. The same method as in Section 3.1.6, except source texts (rather than community
summaries) are shuffled and chunked for the map-reduce summarization stages.

Table 3 shows the results for the average number of extracted claims (i.e., the claim-based measure
of comprehensiveness) per condition. For both the News and Podcast datasets, all global search
conditions (C0-C3) and source text summarization (TS) had greater comprehensiveness than vector
RAG (SS). The differences were statistically significant (p <.05) in all cases. These findings align
with the LLM-based win rates from Experiment 1.
Table 4 contains the results for the average number of clusters, the claim-based measure of diver-
sity. For the Podcast dataset, all global search conditions had significantly greater diversity than SS
across all distance thresholds (p<.05), consistent with the win rates observed in Experiment 1. For
the News dataset, however, only C0 significantly outperformed SS across all distance thresholds

To extract factual claims, we used Claimify (Metropolitansky and Larson, 2025), an LLM-based
method that identifies sentences in an answer containing at least one factual claim, then decomposes
these sentences into simple, self-contained factual claims. We applied Claimify to the answers
generated under the conditions from Experiment 1. After removing duplicate claims from each
answer, we extracted 47,075 unique claims, with an average of 31 claims per answer.
We defined two metrics, with higher values indicating better performance:
1. Comprehensiveness: Measured as the average number of claims extracted from the an-
swers generated under each condition.
2. Diversity: Measured by clustering the claims for each answer and calculating the average
number of clusters.
For clustering, we followed the approach described by Padmakumar and He (2024), which involved
using Scikit-learn’s implementation of agglomerative clustering (Pedregosa et al., 2011). Clusters
were merged through “complete” linkage, meaning they were combined only if the maximum dis-
tance between their farthest points was less than or equal to a predefined distance threshold. The
distance metric used was 1 − ROUGE-L. Since the distance threshold influences the number of
clusters, we report results across a range of thresholds.

final_answer:
The question asks for the number of context units and token counts for two specific methods—root-level community summaries (C0) and source-text summarization (TS)—across two datasets—Podcast and News.

The definitions for the conditions are found in Section 4.1.2: C0 uses root-level community summaries, which are the fewest in number [4]. TS applies a map-reduce approach directly to source texts, which are shuffled and chunked [4][5]. Table 2 provides the specific figures for context units, token counts, and percentage of maximum token count for these conditions on both datasets [1][3].

Comparing the figures from Table 2:
- **Podcast Dataset**:
  - C0: 34 Units, 26,657 Tokens [1][3].
  - TS: 1,669 Units, 1,014,611 Tokens [1][3].
- **News Dataset**:
  - C0: 55 Units, 39,770 Tokens [1][3].
  - TS: 3,197 Units, 1,707,694 Tokens [1][3].

**Improvements (Efficiency)**: C0 requires dramatically fewer resources than TS in both datasets.
- On Podcast, C0 uses 34 units compared to TS's 1,669 units, and 26,657 tokens compared to TS's 1,014,611 tokens [1][3].
- On News, C0 uses 55 units compared to TS's 3,197 units, and 39,770 tokens compared to TS's 1,707,694 tokens [1][3].
- The text states that C0 requires 9x-43x fewer tokens per query than the most resource-intensive approach (TS) [1][2]. Specifically, C0 uses only 2.6% of the max tokens for Podcast and 2.3% for News, whereas TS uses 100% of the max tokens in both cases [1].

Consistency Check:
- "Higher" resource usage for TS: 1,014,611 > 26,657 (Podcast) and 1,707,694 > 39,770 (News) [1].
- "Lower" resource usage for C0: 34 < 1,669 (Podcast units) and 55 < 3,197 (News units) [1].
- The statement that C0 requires over 97% fewer tokens than TS is supported by the percentages (2.6% vs 100% for Podcast; 2.3% vs 100% for News), implying a reduction of ~97.4% and ~97.7% respectively [1].

Source Citations:
- Figures for Podcast and News units and tokens: Table 2 in [1] and [3].
- Definitions of C0 and TS: Section 4.1.2 in [4] and [5].
- General statement on token reduction (9x-43x, >97%): Page 10 text in [1] and [2].

All requested data points (units and tokens for C0 and TS on Podcast and News) are present in Table 2.

**Comparison Table**

| Condition | Dataset | Context Units | Tokens | % Max Tokens |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **C0** | Podcast | 34 | 26,657 | 2.6 |
| **TS** | Podcast | 1,669 | 1,014,611 | 100 |
| **C0** | News | 55 | 39,770 | 2.3 |
| **TS** | News | 3,197 | 1,707,694 | 100 |

**Analysis**
The root-level community summaries (C0) utilize significantly fewer context units and tokens than the source-text summarization (TS) method on both datasets. On the Podcast dataset, C0 uses 34 units and 26,657 tokens, whereas TS uses 1,669 units and 1,014,611 tokens [1][3]. On the News dataset, C0 uses 55 units and 39,770 tokens, whereas TS uses 3,197 units and 1,707,694 tokens [1][3]. C0 represents only 2.6% and 2.3% of the maximum token count for Podcast and News respectively, while TS utilizes 100% of the maximum token count in both cases [1]. The text confirms that C0 requires dramatically fewer tokens, citing a 9x-43x reduction and stating that C0 required over 97% fewer tokens compared to TS [1][2].

Numbers that could not be checked against the cited pages of the original text: 97.4%, 97.7%.
